notes.decision: Translated 'the three Zones.' ⲍⲱⲛⲏ (Greek ζώνη) is the standard cosmological 'Girdle/Zone' (cf. accumulated vocab ⲧⲍⲱⲛⲏ). The chapter enumerates three: (1) the five powers of Darkness in the Five Sons of First Man, (2) the Five Sons of the Living Spirit, (3) the firmament with the King of Honor.

Read as ⲡⲥⲁ-ⲛ-ϩⲟⲩⲛ 'the inside, within' — Lyc form. 'A Zone of the inside of another Zone' = nested-within construction. Translation 'within another Zone' captures the Manichaean image of concentric cosmic girdles.

Compound ⲣⲙ̄-ⲁⲛ-ⲧⲡⲉ = 'man of heaven, heavenly one.' 'The five heaven-men, the sons of the Man (= First Man).' The Five Sons of the First Man are the heavenly elements; here they constitute the Zone in which the dark powers are bound.

ϫⲁⲗϫ = qualitative 'fettered, squeezed, compressed' (cf. ϩⲉⲝϩⲁⲝⲧ in vocab); ⲉⲥⲙⲏⲡ = 'reckoned, included.' Together: the Enmity (= the dark powers) is held compressed and reckoned within the Five Sons.

ϩⲣϥⲟⲣⲉ analyzed as a Lyc verbal noun built on Greek ϥⲟⲣⲉⲓ 'wear, bear' — 'comes-wearing/being-borne in the holy ones.' Translated 'comes to be worn in the holy ones' to preserve the indwelling-as-garment image (cf. ⲣⲫⲟⲣⲉ in accumulated vocab for the First Man wearing his Five Sons as armor).

Per accumulated glossary, ⲡⲣⲙⲛⲉⲥ = 'the Ancient One.' In this anthropological context (the Light-Mind binding the X within the body of flesh) the term clearly designates the Manichaean 'Old Man' (palaios anthrōpos) — the dark, fleshly self that the Light-Mind subdues and binds within the body. 'Ancient One' retained for terminological consistency, but the Pauline 'old man' resonance is intended.

Obscure form. Possibly Lyc reflex of ⲉϣϣⲉ 'it is fitting/necessary,' or a frozen demonstrative-deictic 'behold.' Translated '[it stands fixed]' tentatively — the disciple is summarizing what follows from what the apostle taught.

Lexeme uncertain. Context (paired with the next line's 'unchanging, unmeasured great god' and 'how does he become confined in the smallness of the body') requires a noun for change/variation/alteration that the disciple observes phenomenologically in the saint, contrasting with the Light-Mind's intrinsic immutability. Tentatively 'alteration.' Possibly related to ⲡⲱϣⲥ 'split, divide' or to ⲃⲗ̄ⲥ̄ 'weakness/decay.'

Verbal lexeme of uncertain root, paralleling ⲛⲁⲧϣⲓⲃⲉ ⲛⲁⲧϣⲓ ('unchanging, unmeasured') as predicate of the Mind's incarnation. Context (within the smallness of the body) demands a verb of confinement/restriction. Translated 'be confined' — possibly Lyc reflex of a verb of narrowing or dwelling-in-tight-space.

ϩⲥⲁⲧϥ̄ analyzed as Lyc reflex of ϩⲁⲣⲁⲧϥ̄ / ϩⲁⲧⲏϥ 'beside him, near him.' The disciple's third question concerns the relational mode of the Mind's presence in/beside the holy person. Translated 'whose Mind is beside him.'
